papers.summary: Spectral weight decay applies additive singular-value shrinkage. The paper reports lower effective rank and better SVD-LLM compression at matched validation loss, plus cleaner test accuracy under label noise.
papers.relevance: Direct match for spectral regularization, low-rank compressibility, proximal methods, and memorization under label noise.

evidence.quote: spectral weight decay lowers effective rank and improves SVD-LLM compression at matched validation loss.
Regularization coefficients are calibrated in separate tuning runs using final clean-validation accuracy

papers.title: Spectral Weight Decay: Inducing Low-Rank Structure in Neural Network Weights

papers.summary: ORCA applies soft orthogonality regularization early in LLM training, then removes it. In the inspected LLaMA comparisons, it reduced final validation loss relative to Muon at matched token budgets.
papers.relevance: Directly tests how spectral shaping affects effective rank and LLM optimization.

evidence.quote: applies strong but temporary soft orthogonality regularization early in training, then removes it.
Compared with Muon, ORCA reduces the final loss by 0.0194 at 350M and 0.0244 at 1.3B

papers.title: ORCA: The Annealed Spectral Conditioning Optimizer for Faster, Better LLM Training

papers.summary: Spectrally Targeted Muon isolates singular subspaces using Newton–Schulz projections. Its NanoGPT analysis finds that effective rank and validation loss need not move together.
papers.relevance: Direct match for Muon, Newton–Schulz methods, and the relationship between spectra and optimization.

evidence.quote: It isolates the relevant singular subspaces with projections computed by Newton-Schulz iteration on a shifted Gram matrix, so no SVD is needed.
the bottom targeted variants keep Muon’s rank without matching its loss

papers.title: Spectrally Targeted Muon

papers.summary: Controlled LoRA experiments separate frozen-factor choice from spectral-band choice. At rank 2, the factor contrast exceeds the band contrast in four complete task–model comparisons, but weakens at higher rank.
papers.relevance: Direct evidence on low-rank factor optimization and spectral placement in language-model fine-tuning.

evidence.quote: We use a two-by-two design: freeze A or B, each on the top or bottom band, while retaining the same pretrained model, data, adapted modules and training budget.
The factor contrast decreases along the complete OpenBookQA rank sweep, becoming comparable to the band contrast at rank 16.

papers.title: Frozen Factor or Spectral Band? Disentangling Two Choices in Low-Rank LoRA

papers.summary: Compares six PEFT methods through task performance, forgetting, and pretrained-weight geometry. Restoring pretrained singular values largely retains task performance in the tested settings.
papers.relevance: Connects singular-value behavior to practical language-model adaptation and retention.

evidence.quote: We study six representative methods, including LoRA, DoRA, PiSSA, MiLoRA, OFT, and HRA, across language-model adaptation and diffusion personalization.
Restoring pretrained singular values largely preserves task performance, while restoring dominant components consistently yields the largest mean reduction in forgetting

papers.title: Are Parameter-Efficient Fine-tuning Methods Really Different?

papers.summary: LoGRA uses low-rank gradient sketches for LLM RL post-training. Inspected results report average per-GPU memory falling from 31.82 to 17.29 GiB at 7B, with similar update rates to dense Adam.
papers.relevance: Directly informs low-rank training-memory and throughput tradeoffs, although not in pretraining.

evidence.quote: average memory decreases from 9.18 to 7.18 GiB at 1.5B and from 31.82 to 17.29 GiB at 7B
End-to-end update rates are similar where both methods complete training: 55.44 versus 54.28 updates/h at 1.5B and 25.73 versus 25.28 updates/h at 7B for LoGRA and Dense, respectively.

papers.title: LoGRA: Scaling LLM Reinforcement Learning with Low-Rank Gradient Sketches

papers.summary: Describes reversible archiving of tool observations in a Python agent harness. An exploratory case reduced cumulative input tokens, but another case showed no saving and an earlier continuation had lower assessed quality.
papers.relevance: Directly applicable to explicit context management in a handwritten research-digest agent.

evidence.quote: A Python harness exposes batch archival and explicit recovery without task-specific model training
A contrasting application-development pair produced no context or cost saving, and an earlier continuation exhibited lower manually assessed quality despite reduced context.

papers.title: Agent-Controlled Forgetting for Tool-Using Agents: Reversible Context Curation in Practice

limitations: The quoted results are authors’ reported findings, not independently verified reproductions.
LoGRA evaluates RL post-training, so its memory–quality tradeoff should not be assumed to transfer to LLM pretraining.
The agent-context study is exploratory and reports mixed outcomes.
X analysis was disabled; no attention claims are made.
